module_summary: system.cpp is the menu-side platform core: embedded IRX loading (sysLoadModuleBuffer), IOP reset, DEV9/PC CARD bus ownership, disc ID, the per-launch IOP module table written to kernel/user RAM (sendIrxKernelRAM), kernel patching and the EE-core launch (sysLaunchLoaderElf), plus POPSTARTER/EMBER/IGR overlay handoffs. sysvmc.cpp holds the memory-card presence check and VMC probe/create logic (genvmc devctl, contiguity ioctl probe); it was split out of system.cpp and kept that file's whole include/constant prelude. tar.h/tar.cpp are a wOPL-derived ustar index/reader used for ART/art.tar covers, CHT/cht.tar cheats and THM/thm_<Name>.tar theme archives, with a sidecar index cache per kind.

reusable_helpers.name: sysLoadModuleBuffer
reusable_helpers.what: loads an embedded IRX blob on the IOP under a lock

reusable_helpers.name: USBA_crc32
reusable_helpers.what: USBAdvance/ul.cfg name CRC32 (table built per call)

reusable_helpers.name: sysCheckMC
reusable_helpers.what: returns the first memory card slot (0/1) whose root opens, else negative

reusable_helpers.name: sysCheckVMCEx
reusable_helpers.what: probe, validate, delete or create a VMC image via genvmc

reusable_helpers.name: sysVMCContiguity
reusable_helpers.what: asks the block driver whether a file is one contiguous fragment

reusable_helpers.name: parseOctal
reusable_helpers.what: parses a fixed-width octal tar header field

reusable_helpers.name: tarRead
reusable_helpers.what: open/seek/read/close one archive member into a buffer

reusable_helpers.name: tarThemeRead
reusable_helpers.what: reads a file that lives inside a THM/thm_X.tar theme archive into a malloc'd NUL-terminated buffer

findings.title: __DECI2_DEBUG code in system.cpp (and its satellites) is compiled by no ps2build configuration
findings.problem: The only places that define __DECI2_DEBUG are the legacy top-level Makefile:340 and ee_core/Makefile:44 (not the build) and a syntax-sweep set in tools/syntax_sweep.py:23; ps2.yaml, tools/build_*.py and the workflows never set it. So the DECI2 reboot buffer, the DECI2 in-game module pair, the kernel-RAM UDNL copy, ResetDECI2/sysInitDECI2 and their prototypes/callers are dead in every shipped or CI-built configuration.
findings.fix: Delete every #ifdef __DECI2_DEBUG block listed (keep the #else side where there is one: the plain SifIopReset, the loop from i = 0, the TTY_UDP/PPC branches as #if/#elif), the sysInitDECI2 prototype and call, and the iopcontrol_special.h includes. The CORE_IRX_DECI2 masks at system.cpp:829 and 1411 then become no-ops and can go too.
findings.benefit: ~95 lines in system.cpp plus ~15 in the satellites removed; no ELF change because the code is preprocessed out today (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Grep -i deci2 over ps2.yaml, tools/*.py, .github/workflows/*.yml: no matches. Grep __DECI2_DEBUG over the repo (excluding docs): defines only in Makefile:340, ee_core/Makefile:44, tools/syntax_sweep.py:23; tests at system.cpp:9,316,993,1025,1042,1068,1191,1400, sysvmc.cpp:7, sysneutrino.cpp:7, sysdisc.cpp:9, system.h:122, opl.cpp:2056, debug.cpp:20,25, ee_core/src/iopmgr.c:183. Brief section 2 states the Makefile tree is legacy and not the build.

findings.title: sysLaunchDisc prelude (SYS_DISC_* budgets, time.h, delaythread.h) copied unused into system.cpp, sysvmc.cpp and sysneutrino.cpp
findings.problem: SYS_DISC_DETECT_MS/REDETECT_MS/NODISC_MS, clock() and DelayThread are used only in sysdisc.cpp (134-206), yet the same 12-13 line block with its long comment sits in three other files where nothing reads it (system.cpp still needs delaythread.h for line 504). sysvmc.cpp also kept system.cpp's whole include list (gui, lang, launchdiag, eth/hdd/bdm/mmce support, pad, OSDHistory, renderman, extern_irx, ee_core modules/coreconfig, pggsm, sema_lock, cheatman, xparam, rawatch, ds34) although its code only uses system.h, ioman.h (LOG), fileXio, usbhdfsd-common, ps2sdkapi_compat and genvmc.h.
findings.fix: Delete the SYS_DISC_* constants and time.h include from system.cpp, sysvmc.cpp and sysneutrino.cpp, and delaythread.h from sysvmc.cpp and sysneutrino.cpp; keep them only in sysdisc.cpp. Trim sysvmc.cpp's include block to the headers its code uses.
findings.benefit: ~38 lines of copied constants/comments removed, ~25 more include lines in sysvmc.cpp; constexpr ints emit no code, so no ELF change (INFERRED); slightly faster compiles
findings.evidence: Grep SYS_DISC_|DelayThread|clock(|CLOCKS_PER_SEC over src/platform: uses only in sysdisc.cpp:126-206 and DelayThread at system.cpp:504; definitions only in system.cpp:17-25, sysvmc.cpp:15-23, sysneutrino.cpp:15-23, sysdisc.cpp:17-25. Read all of sysvmc.cpp: its symbols are LOG, open/read/lseek/unlink, DIR, fileXio*, ps2sdk_get_iop_fd, USBMASS_IOCTL_*, createVMCparam_t, vmc_superblock_t, SYS_VMC_*. The exact minimal include set is INFERRED (transitive includes not compiled).

findings.title: Unused declarations in system.cpp: local createVMCparam_t, ELF_MAGIC, guiEnd/menuEnd/thmEnd/rmEnd prototypes
findings.problem: createVMCparam_t is a stale local copy (no VMC_flags) left after the VMC code moved to sysvmc.cpp, which uses genvmc.h's type; ELF_MAGIC is never referenced; the four teardown prototypes are never called in system.cpp (opl.cpp calls them via gui.h/menusys.h/themes.h/renderman.h). sysPlaceIgrOverlay meanwhile hand-checks the ELF magic byte by byte and uses a literal 1 for PT_LOAD next to the ELF_PT_LOAD constant.
findings.fix: Delete the typedef, ELF_MAGIC and the four prototypes. Optionally use ELF_PT_LOAD at 1319 and 1331.
findings.benefit: ~13 lines removed; no ELF change (declarations only)
findings.evidence: Grep createVMCparam_t|ELF_MAGIC|ELF_PT_LOAD|guiEnd|menuEnd|thmEnd|rmEnd over src/platform: createVMCparam_t only system.cpp:76 (typedef) and sysvmc.cpp:263 (uses genvmc.h type, include at sysvmc.cpp:65); ELF_MAGIC only system.cpp:99; ELF_PT_LOAD used at 1642; the four prototypes appear in system.cpp only at 132-135; real declarations in include/gui.h:81, menusys.h:115, themes.h:342, renderman.h:79.

findings.title: USBA_crc32 table crctab[0x400] is four times the 256 entries it uses
findings.problem: The table loop fills indices 0..255 and the lookup index is byte ^ (crc>>24 & 0xFF), at most 255, so entries 256..1023 of the static unsigned int crctab[0x400] are never touched.
findings.benefit: 768 x 4 = 3072 bytes of .bss saved (INFERRED from the declaration)
findings.evidence: Read system.cpp:465-492: writes crctab[255 - table] for table 0..255; reads crctab[byte ^ ((crc >> 24) & 0xFF)] with unsigned char byte. Grep crctab: no other use in the repo's src. Callers of USBA_crc32: supportbase.cpp:656,1226,1473 and ethsupport.cpp:1434.

findings.title: sendIrxKernelRAM repeats the two-line module-table append 37 times, and the UDPFS chains duplicate smap+ministack
findings.problem: Every module goes into irxptr_tab with the same pair 'irxptr_tab[modcount].info = size_X | SET_OPL_MOD_ID(ID); irxptr_tab[modcount++].ptr = (void *)&X;' (37 occurrences). The BDM_UFS and UDPFS_FILES branches each append the same udpfs_smap and udpfs_ministack pair before their one differing module.
findings.fix: Add one function-local macro (or static inline) that appends {size, id, ptr} and use it for every row; merge the two UDPFS branches into one block guarded by (CORE_IRX_UDPFS | CORE_IRX_UDPFS_FILES) that appends smap+ministack and then udpfs_bd or udpfs_fhi.
findings.justification: The helper is one line and replaces 37 two-line pairs with one-line calls, a net removal of ~35 lines, and removes the chance of a pair whose info and ptr name different modules.
findings.benefit: ~38 lines removed net; code size roughly unchanged (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Grep -c 'irxptr_tab[modcount].info' system.cpp = 37, all within 857-1011. Read 917-934: both branches append udpfs_smap then udpfs_ministack, then udpfs_bd (BDM_UFS) or udpfs_fhi (UDPFS_FILES); the flags are set by mutually exclusive mode strings at 802-805 so order is preserved. Risk Med: touches the in-game module table.

findings.title: Small dead parameters and redundant branches in system.cpp launch code
findings.problem: patchlist_t.mode is "" in every iop_patch_list row, so the mode test at 733 (and the mode_str argument to addIopPatch) never filters; GetModStorageLocation's compatFlags parameter is never read; the BDM_ATA_MODE branch sets CORE_IRX_HDD exactly like the final else at 806-807; sysPrintEECoreConfig (debug builds) logs enforceLanguage twice.
findings.fix: Delete the mode field, the mode clause and addIopPatch's mode_str parameter; drop the compatFlags parameter; delete the BDM_ATA_MODE else-if; delete the second enforceLanguage LOG.
findings.benefit: ~10 lines and 7 string literals removed; a few bytes of .rodata (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read iop_patch_list 714-723 (all mode ""), addIopPatch 725-741 (only caller 1020), GetModStorageLocation 755-769 (only caller 1398; body never reads compatFlags), mode chain 784-807, sysPrintEECoreConfig 1204-1235.

findings.title: sysCheckVMCEx reads and validates the VMC superblock with two copies of the same loop
findings.problem: When the caller passes no superblock and the size is whole-MB, lines 168-185 seek, loop-read a vmc_superblock_t into a local and check magic/type/geometry; lines 188-216 repeat the same seek, loop-read and checks into vmc_superblock. The function already redirects a NULL pointer to a local (autoSuperblock, 161-163) for the format probe.
findings.fix: Always point vmc_superblock at the local autoSuperblock when the caller passed NULL, read it once with the second loop, and keep the first block only as the early-return decision based on that single validation result.
findings.benefit: ~15 lines removed and one fewer seek+read of 512+ bytes per probe on a whole-MB card (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read sysvmc.cpp:138-279. The two loops at 172-178 and 192-198 are line-for-line the same apart from the target buffer; the checks differ only in that the first requires page_size == 512 and returns early. .github/scripts/test_vmc_preserve_existing.py exercises these return codes and would cover the merge. Risk Med: VMC create/replace path.

findings.title: tarFind/tarFindExact and tarFindPrefix/tarFindPrefixExact duplicate their search loops; the ART/CFG/CHT prefix strip is written three times
findings.problem: The Exact variants differ from the plain ones only in their entry guard (s_isExact required instead of cleared + lazy device sweep); the name loop (479-501 vs 538-555) and the prefix loop (516-531 vs 562-573) are identical, and the './' + 'ART/'|'CFG/'|'CHT/' strip appears at 349-352, 480-483 and 539-542.
findings.fix: Move the two loops into static searchName(kind, name) and searchPrefix(kind, prefix) and the strip into one static stripKindPrefix(); the four public functions keep only their guard and call the helper.
findings.benefit: ~30 lines removed; a few hundred bytes of .text (INFERRED: two duplicated loops of string compares)
findings.evidence: Read tar.cpp:467-574 side by side; duplicate leads tar.cpp:477-501==537-555 and 514-531==561-573 confirmed. tests/host/test_tar.cpp:55-95 exercises tarFindExact/tarFindPrefixExact and would cover the refactor; callers artload.cpp:89-91, supportbase.cpp:1761-1769, tar.cpp:676.

findings.title: tarClose duplicates tarInvalidate and is used only by host tests; tarLoadFromAnyDevice is exported but only called inside tar.cpp
findings.problem: tarClose and tarInvalidate have the same body (tarCloseInternal + clear s_inactive); production calls only tarInvalidate (settingsio.cpp:2480, guisettings.cpp:1804) and tarClose appears only in tests/host/test_tar.cpp:81,92,159. tarLoadFromAnyDevice's only callers are tar.cpp:476 and 513.
findings.fix: Delete tarClose and switch the host test to tarInvalidate; make tarLoadFromAnyDevice static and drop its prototype.
findings.benefit: ~8 lines removed; no ELF change claimed (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Grep tarClose|tarInvalidate|tarLoadFromAnyDevice over the repo: tarClose defined tar.cpp:460, declared tar.h:75, used tests/host/test_tar.cpp:81,92,159 only; tarInvalidate calls settingsio.cpp:2480, guisettings.cpp:1804; tarLoadFromAnyDevice called tar.cpp:476,513 only (plus tar.h:73).

findings.title: TAR_KIND_CFG is wired to nothing in the program, and the tar.h/tar.cpp banners still say only ART is wired
findings.problem: No source under src/ references TAR_KIND_CFG or TarEntryCfg; the kind is kept 'so it can be wired later' and is exercised only by tests/host/test_tar.cpp:99-103. The banners claim RiptOPL wires ONLY the ART kind, but CHT is live (supportbase.cpp:1761-1784) and THM theme archives are live (themes.cpp, sfx.cpp, bgm.cpp, textures.cpp, fntsys.cpp).
findings.fix: Delete TAR_KIND_CFG, TarEntryCfg, its gTarInfo row, the 'CFG/' alternative in the prefix strip and the CFG part of the host test; rewrite the two banners in one line each to say ART, CHT and THM are used.
findings.benefit: ~12 lines removed and stale guidance corrected; ~20 bytes .rodata (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Grep TAR_KIND_CFG|TarEntryCfg over the repo: tar.h:57,67, tar.cpp:61, tests/host/test_tar.cpp:99,100,103,159 only. Grep TAR_KIND_CHT: supportbase.cpp:1761,1769,1777,1784. tarTheme* callers in themes.cpp:1422,1447,1939, sfx.cpp:95,222, bgm.cpp:561, textures.cpp:1122,1321, fntsys.cpp:382.

findings.title: include/tar.h included with a 'tarInvalidate' comment in ten files that use nothing from it
findings.problem: These files include tar.h (most with the comment 'tarInvalidate -- re-arm the .tar probe') but contain no tar* call or Tar/TAR_ identifier besides that comment; only settingsio.cpp and guisettings.cpp call tarInvalidate.
findings.evidence: Grep -c '\btar[A-Z]|TAR_|Tar[A-Z]' over src: count 1 (the include comment itself) for menuitems, guiwait, guimodal, guigameid, gui, appscan, autolaunch, lwnbdctl, opl; texcache.cpp has 0 matches yet includes tar.h at line 13. Real users: settingsio.cpp (2), guisettings.cpp (3), artload, supportbase, themes, textures, sfx, bgm, fntsys.
